familySensitivity.changedAxis: current check-in state for a strength-priority athlete with no wearable data
familySensitivity.rationale: The planner demonstrates clean, well-calibrated sensitivity across subjective-only states: full strength programming under normal readiness, acute deloading followed by Week-2 rebound under occupational fatigue, and strict mechanical guardrail substitution (low-load strength and trunk maintenance) when shoulder/back symptoms flare.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery/time state and subjective-vs-wearable disagreement for a health-and-fat-loss evergreen athlete with Garmin data
familySensitivity.rationale: The family handles baseline evergreen health programming, concordant adverse recovery, and the 30-minute time ceiling very effectively. However, in the discordant case (fresh subjective check-in paired with adverse Garmin metrics), the initial two-day Total Rest response is nearly indistinguishable from concordant adverse recovery, showing mild over-reliance on objective autonomic suppression over strong subjective readiness.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery state for a former high-level endurance athlete whose present training is intermittent
familySensitivity.rationale: Strong calibration across the family axis: historical elite status never triggers reckless Week-1 volume, genuine physiological/subjective distress triggers a disciplined multi-day recovery ramp, and isolated low motivation is appropriately ignored as a physiological red flag.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery, today-specific modality preference, and already-trained state for an evergreen balanced-performance generalist
familySensitivity.rationale: Highly accurate state differentiation across all four perturbations. In particular, the planner cleanly distinguishes same-day execution (`alreadyTrainedToday: true`) from systemic fatigue (`adverse_recovery`), resting only on Day 1 and re-allocating the primary strength stimulus to Thursday rather than suppressing the rest of the microcycle.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery/time state with a standing running restriction, heavy-lower-body guardrail, and no training equipment
familySensitivity.rationale: Exceptional hard-gate enforcement and state sensitivity: no restricted modality (Running), unavailable equipment, or heavy lower-body session ever leaks into any of the three 14-day plans, while adverse recovery and Day-1 time compression are handled proportionally.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery/time state for a health-priority athlete who cannot run and prefers walking
familySensitivity.rationale: The planner demonstrates clean, reliable sensitivity across all three state variations for the walking-preferred, running-restricted health persona. Running is completely excluded in all cases, walking is scheduled as substantive aerobic training rather than recovery filler, adverse biometrics trigger an immediate 3-day down-regulation before graded re-entry, and the 30-minute time cap downscales session durations while preserving both aerobic walking and resistance training.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: current recovery, motivation, and recent hard-session density for an endurance athlete with a genuinely established current training base
familySensitivity.rationale: The family exhibits strong discrimination across all four physiological and psychological contexts: adverse recovery withdraws quality work and inserts early rest; isolated low motivation does not falsely trigger recovery gating; and recent two-hard-session load density down-regulates immediate load and shifts the next quality run back by an extra recovery day despite green morning biometrics.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: recovery, local mechanical constraint, today-specific modality preference, and time availability for a cycling-primary hybrid athlete
familySensitivity.rationale: The planner excels on safety-critical and guardrail axes: adverse recovery down-regulates intensity cleanly, local-tissue pain and guardrails override glowing Garmin biometrics without losing low-impact Zone 2 cycling, and a today-specific strength preference does not hijack the week into strength-primary programming. However, Day 1 does not differentiate between preferredModalityToday='Cycling' (baseline) and 'Strength', and under the 35-minute time cap the planner over-relies on 30-minute walks (7 walks vs 4 rides) despite 20-30 minute indoor cycling templates being eligible.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: A/B/C event priority for the same established runner, same scheduled 10K, same race date, same recovery and same current training history
familySensitivity.rationale: The planner demonstrates textbook monotonic sensitivity across A/B/C event priorities with all other variables held constant: Priority A initiates a full two-week taper (5 rest days, 20-40 min taper sharpening replacing Week 2 build workouts); Priority B executes a secondary mini-taper (retaining the D-7 Steady-State Tempo Run before sharpening at D-4); and Priority C trains through the race week with both D-7 Tempo (30-50 min) and D-4 Race-Pace Specificity (40-75 min) while still resting at D-1.

familySensitivity.changedAxis: recovery, weekday capacity, and race proximity for one established Olympic-distance triathlete
familySensitivity.rationale: The planner maintains strict three-discipline fidelity (Swimming, Cycling, Running) across every variant while adapting cleanly to each changed axis: adverse recovery inserts 3 days of rest/mobility followed by modified easy swim/bike/run re-entry; the 45-minute weekday cap trims Mon-Fri session durations to <=45 min while keeping weekend endurance sessions intact; and the 14-day taper window strips out heavy threshold/race-endurance/lower-body-strength load in favor of technique and pre-race openers.

caseScores.rationale: Treats the subjective-only check-in as sufficient decision evidence without penalizing missing wearable fields. Delivers a coherent 3-4x/week strength-focused schedule using free weights and bodyweight templates while avoiding deprioritized running and cycling. Slightly dilutes maximal bench/deadlift specificity by using a bodyweight full-body session on Day 3 and a pull-up practice template on Day 5 (which assumes pull-up bar access), plus one brisk walk in Week 2.
suggestedChanges: Prefer free-weight lower/hinge or compound full-body strength templates over bodyweight maintenance and pull-up-bar-dependent sessions when free weights are available and maximal bench/deadlift strength is the primary goal.

caseScores.rationale: Respects high occupational fatigue (8/10) and soreness (7/10) from the subjective check-in by prescribing Total Rest on Day 1 and down-scaling Day 2 to a 20-30 minute reduced strength maintenance session before returning to full-body push/pull strength on Day 7 and in Week 2. However, scheduling three consecutive brisk walks on Days 4-6 is somewhat non-specific for a manual-labor strength athlete who already accumulates high occupational physical load.
suggestedChanges: Replace one of the consecutive mid-week modified walking days (Days 4-6) with rest or light mobility/trunk work for manual-labor strength personas recovering from occupational fatigue.

caseScores.rationale: Reacts decisively and safely to the active pain flag and shoulder/back guardrails (avoid_overhead_pressing, avoid_heavy_spinal_loading): takes two rest days up front and substitutes all heavy compound push/pull sessions with alternating Low-load Strength and Trunk Maintenance (3x/week) and brisk walks. Preserves strength training frequency without violating mechanical restrictions or over-medicalizing the flare.

Provides an adherence-friendly, evergreen mix of full-body resistance training and brisk walking within the 60-minute cap, without inventing race periodization or nutritional claims. Week 1 balances two full-body strength sessions with two walks and mobility, though Week 2 drops strength down to a single 20-30 minute reduced maintenance session alongside five walks.
suggestedChanges: Maintain at least two resistance training exposures in Week 2 to better support lean-mass retention for the health and fat-loss goal.

caseScores.rationale: Appropriately down-regulates the initial three days to rest and mobility in response to concordant subjective fatigue and adverse Garmin metrics (sleep score 52, RHR +7, HRV -14, body battery 24), then ramps through brisk walking back to full-body strength on Day 7. One minor preference drift occurs on Day 10 (2026-09-09), where a Light Base Run is scheduled despite Running not being in the persona's preferred modalities (Strength, Walking, Cycling).
suggestedChanges: Keep aerobic modified sessions aligned with preferred modalities (Walking or Cycling) rather than introducing Running for a higher-body-mass fat-loss persona.

caseScores.rationale: Strictly honors the 30-minute time ceiling across the entire 14-day schedule (every session has durationMax <= 30) while preserving both resistance training (15-25 minute bodyweight strength 2x in Week 1, 1x in Week 2) and regular 30-minute brisk walks.

When subjective readiness is very fresh (readiness 8, sleep quality 8, fatigue 2, motivation 8) but Garmin recovery metrics are adverse, the planner still prescribes two consecutive Total Rest days on Days 1-2—identical to the concordant adverse recovery case—before resuming brisk walks on Days 3-5 and full-body strength on Day 6. While capping high intensity is prudent under autonomic strain, two days of complete rest slightly over-weights the wearable signal over the athlete's fresh subjective readiness.
suggestedChanges: Under conflicting fresh-subjective and adverse-wearable signals, prefer a low-strain active session (such as a 30-minute brisk walk or mobility flow) on Day 1 or Day 2 instead of two consecutive Total Rest days.

caseScores.rationale: Correctly anchors Week 1 training dose to sparse present-day history rather than former elite biathlon background, prescribing controlled 30-minute easy running, brisk walking, and two full-body strength sessions. Two minor flaws: Day 1 selects full-body strength despite preferredModalityToday being Running, and Week 2 jumps from a single 30-minute easy run in Week 1 to four runs including two 30-50 minute Steady-State Tempo Runs within three days (Friday and Sunday).
suggestedChanges: Honor preferredModalityToday ('Running') on Day 1 when readiness is high and no constraints block running.
Cap moderate/tempo running to a single exposure in Week 2 when rebuilding from intermittent/sparse history, keeping the second weekend session as an easy base run.

caseScores.rationale: Prioritizes current adverse recovery (readiness 4, sleep score 52, RHR +7, HRV -14) over historical competitive status and high motivation (8/10). Prescribes two rest days and mobility before easing back via light base running, walking, and walk/jog intervals, delaying full strength until Day 7 and limiting Week 2 to a single moderate tempo run.

Correctly treats isolated low motivation (2/10) with healthy physiological and fatigue signals (readiness 7, fatigue 3, sleep 80, HRV 42) as non-pathological, maintaining the productive baseline training structure without unnecessary forced rest. Shares the minor baseline behaviors of scheduling Strength on Day 1 despite a Running preference and clustering two tempo runs at the end of Week 2.
suggestedChanges: Honor today's Running modality preference on Day 1 and replace one of the two Week-2 tempo runs with an easy base run.

caseScores.rationale: Delivers a well-structured evergreen generalist plan combining two full-body strength sessions and two aerobic sessions in Week 1, followed by progressive running and maintenance strength in Week 2, all within the 60-minute cap. Week 2 tilts slightly toward running (four runs including two tempo sessions vs one reduced strength maintenance session).
suggestedChanges: Include a second full-body strength session in Week 2 rather than two Steady-State Tempo Runs 48 hours apart to keep endurance and strength evenly balanced.

caseScores.rationale: Reacts appropriately to concordant adverse subjective and wearable recovery signals with two days of Total Rest and a mobility session before stepping back through easy aerobic work into Sunday full-body strength and a balanced Week 2.

Satisfies today's explicit Strength preference (`str_full_01` on Day 1) while preserving the multi-day balance between running and resistance training across the 14-day horizon without turning the plan into strength-only programming.

Exemplary handling of `alreadyTrainedToday: true`: prescribes Total Rest on Day 1 to avoid duplicate same-day loading, resumes normal easy running on Day 2 (`end_easy_02`), and cleanly shifts the displaced primary free-weight strength session (`str_full_01`) to Day 4 (Thursday) and Week 2 Thursday so weekly strength and endurance coverage are fully preserved.

Strictly respects all stacked hard constraints across the 14-day horizon—zero running sessions, zero equipment requirements, and no heavy lower-body loading—while sustaining a productive health routine of twice-weekly bodyweight full-body strength (`str_full_02`), brisk walks (`end_walk_01`), and mobility.

Layers acute recovery protection (Days 1-2 Total Rest, Day 3 mobility, Days 4-6 modified 30-minute walks) cleanly on top of the standing running restriction, lower-body guardrail, and zero-equipment constraint before resuming bodyweight strength on Day 7 and in Week 2.

Responds to the 30-minute time window on Day 1 by scaling Bodyweight Full Body Strength (`str_full_02`) down from 30-45 minutes to 15-25 minutes, preserving the resistance stimulus and all standing injury/equipment guardrails without dropping the session.

Strictly respects the running restriction with zero running leakage across the 14-day horizon, treating brisk continuous walking (30-60 min) as genuine aerobic endurance training alongside 2 weekly full-body strength sessions for sustainable health-focused fitness. Minor deduction on preference fit because Day 1 schedules full-body strength despite preferredModalityToday being Walking.
suggestedChanges: Honor preferredModalityToday ('Walking') on Day 1 when readiness is normal and shift the opening full-body strength session to Day 2.
Break up the 3 consecutive walking days at the end of Week 2 (Sep 11-13) with one rest day to stay strictly within the 4-5 session weekly commitment.

caseScores.rationale: Responds proportionately to acute subjective and Garmin recovery suppression (sleep score 52, HRV -14, RHR +7) by prescribing rest and mobility on Days 1-3, then ramping back via 30-minute modified walks before reintroducing full-body strength on Day 7. However, Week 2 clusters five consecutive 30-minute brisk walks (Sep 9-13) after Day 8 strength instead of restoring a balanced 2-strength + 2-3 walk cadence.
suggestedChanges: Replace one of the five consecutive Week 2 brisk walks (e.g., Sep 11 or Sep 12) with a rest day or second strength session once recovery normalizes.

caseScores.rationale: Every session across the 14-day plan strictly obeys the 30-minute ceiling, opening on Day 1 with a 30-minute brisk walk matching preferredModalityToday and preserving twice-weekly resistance training via 15-25 minute full-body sessions without any running leakage.
suggestedChanges: Include a compact free-weight strength template capped at <=30 minutes so free-weight equipment access can still be leveraged under a 30-minute cap.

caseScores.rationale: Schedules one purposeful quality session per week (Steady-State Tempo Run, 30-50 min) buffered by easy runs and rest days with clean sequencing. However, given 12 logged 60-minute runs in the past 28 days and 60-90 min availability, capping standard base runs at 30-40 min and substituting a 30-min walk on Day 2 slightly under-delivers on aerobic volume progression.
suggestedChanges: Allow 45-60 minute continuous aerobic base runs (and a 60-75 min weekend endurance run) for an established runner whose recent 28-day history consistently shows 60-minute easy runs.

caseScores.rationale: Correctly prioritizes acute systemic and subjective recovery suppression (readiness 4, fatigue 7, sleep score 52, HRV -14, RHR +7) over the athlete's strong 28-day training base. Prescribes two rest days and mobility on Days 1-3, eliminates Week 1 tempo work in favor of 30-minute modified easy runs, and restores Steady-State Tempo quality at the end of Week 2.

Properly treats isolated low motivation (motivation 2 with readiness 7, low fatigue/soreness, and normal HRV/RHR/sleep) as non-pathological: starts Day 1 with an approachable 30-40 minute Light Base Run rather than over-reacting with forced rest, and preserves the weekly tempo progression.
suggestedChanges: Maintain 45-60 minute aerobic base runs later in the week once the initial low-friction session is completed.

caseScores.rationale: Despite favorable check-in (readiness 8) and normal Garmin biometrics today, the planner accounts for the two 50-minute hard interval runs in the prior three days (Aug 28 and Aug 30) by down-regulating Day 1 to a modified 30-minute easy run, inserting mobility on Day 4, and delaying the next Steady-State Tempo session until Day 5 (Sep 4), preventing intensity stacking.

Correctly avoids deprioritized running and maintains 1x/week full-body free-weight strength retention alongside 3 weekly cycling rides. However, Day 1 schedules full-body strength despite preferredModalityToday being Cycling (producing an identical plan to the strength-preference case), four 30-minute brisk walks replace cycling aerobic slots despite 90-120 minute windows and indoor/outdoor bike access, and no tempo cycling quality is included despite established tempo ride history.
suggestedChanges: Schedule a cycling session on Day 1 when preferredModalityToday is Cycling.
Replace generic 30-minute Brisk Continuous Walks with Zone 2 cycling or one weekly cycling tempo session for an established cycling-primary athlete with indoor and outdoor bike access.

caseScores.rationale: Excellent response to acute recovery suppression (sleep score 52, HRV -14, RHR +7, fatigue 7): prescribes two rest days and mobility on Days 1-3, re-enters via 20-30 minute modified indoor Zone 2 spins on Days 4-6, and retains strength maintenance (Day 7 full-body and Day 9 reduced full-body) before restoring normal Zone 2 rides in Week 2.

Exemplary handling of conflicting wearable vs mechanical signals: despite sleep score 92, HRV +9, and wake body battery 88, the planner strictly respects painFlag=true and impliedGuardrails ('avoid_high_impact', 'avoid_heavy_lower_body') by resting on Days 1-2, shifting heavy free-weight strength (str_full_01) to lower-load bodyweight strength (str_full_02), and keeping all aerobic work in zero-impact Zone 2 cycling.

Honors preferredModalityToday ('Strength') on Day 1 with Hybrid Full Body Push/Pull (str_full_01) while preventing the week from becoming strength-primary (limiting strength to 1 session per week and keeping endurance volume primary). Slightly held back by the same four 30-minute walking substitutions seen in baseline.
suggestedChanges: Ensure baseline (preferredModalityToday='Cycling') starts with cycling on Day 1 so that switching preferredModalityToday to 'Strength' produces a genuine Day-1 modality swap.

caseScores.rationale: Strictly enforces the 35-minute time cap on every session across the 14-day horizon and retains twice-weekly compact strength (str_full_02, 15-25m). However, even though 20-30 minute indoor Zone 2 Spins (end_easy_01) fit comfortably inside the 35-minute window, the planner schedules 7 Brisk Continuous Walks versus only 4 cycling sessions and opens Day 1 with strength rather than preferredModalityToday ('Cycling').
suggestedChanges: Prefer 20-30 minute indoor Zone 2 Spins (end_easy_01) or short cycling threshold intervals over 30-minute Brisk Continuous Walks (end_walk_01) for a cycling-primary athlete under a 35-minute cap.

caseScores.rationale: Exerts the strongest near-race taper authority for the A-priority 10K: includes 5 total rest days across the 14-day window and replaces longer threshold/race-pace build sessions with brief 20-40 minute Running Taper Sharpening (run_taper_sharpen_01) sessions on Sep 3, 5, and 7 before easy shakeouts in the final days. Minor preference note: schedules one upper-body strength session (str_upper_01) on Sep 10 despite only Running being listed in preferredModalities.
suggestedChanges: Replace the Sep 10 Upper Body Push/Pull session (4 days before the A-priority 10K) with an easy aerobic run or mobility session to stay strictly running-focused during peak week.

caseScores.rationale: Positions Priority B cleanly between A and C: retains more Week 1 training volume and preserves a 30-50 minute Steady-State Tempo Run (end_mod_01) on Sep 7 (7 days out), then transitions into a controlled mini-taper with Running Taper Sharpening (20-40 min) on Sep 10 and rest on Sep 11 and Sep 13.
suggestedChanges: Prefer easy aerobic running over the two modified upper-body strength sessions in Week 1 when preferredModalities contains only Running.

caseScores.rationale: Avoids treating the C-priority 10K as a major peak: retains both the Sep 7 Steady-State Tempo Run (30-50 min) and a full 40-75 minute Running Race-Pace Specificity session (run_race_pace_01) on Sep 10 instead of swapping to short taper sharpening, while still providing a sensible rest day on Sep 13 before the race.
suggestedChanges: Prefer easy aerobic running over the two modified upper-body strength sessions in Week 1 when preferredModalities contains only Running.

caseScores.rationale: Preserves all three race disciplines (Swimming, Cycling, Running) across both weeks with appropriate build specificity 6 weeks out from the Olympic A-event (including Sustained Swim Intervals and weekend Event-Specific Endurance Rides). Slightly penalized on sequencing because Week 1 schedules 7 consecutive active days before clustering both rest days in Week 2 (Sep 10-11), and running volume is somewhat light relative to the athlete's 60-minute run history.
suggestedChanges: Place at least one rest day inside Week 1 rather than running 7 consecutive active days (Aug 31-Sep 6) and clustering two rest days on Sep 10-11.
Honor preferredModalityToday ('Cycling') on Day 1 by swapping the Day 1 swim and Day 2 ride.

caseScores.rationale: Exemplary multi-discipline recovery adaptation: protects Days 1-3 with two rest days and active mobility in response to poor sleep (52), depressed HRV (-14), and elevated RHR (+7), then re-enters via modified easy sessions across all three distinct disciplines on Days 4-6 (Easy Aerobic Swim, Outdoor Zone 2 Ride, Light Base Run) before resuming threshold swim and race-specific bike quality in Week 2.

Every weekday session strictly obeys the 45-minute cap (scaling Sustained Swim Intervals to 35-45 min, Light Base Runs to 30-40 min, and Zone 2 Rides to 20-30 min) while utilizing the 90-minute weekend capacity for the 50-90 minute Event-Specific Endurance Ride and 30-60 minute Sunday swim, preserving all three triathlon disciplines.

Demonstrates clear taper restraint relative to baseline: removes the 50-90 minute Event-Specific Endurance Rides, Sustained Swim Intervals, and Lower Body Strength & Power, replacing them with Easy Aerobic Swims, Pool Swim Technique (25-45m), Pre-Race Openers (20-40m), and short shakeouts while keeping all three disciplines active. However, Week 2 schedules 7 consecutive active days (Sep 7-13) right into the Sep 14 race without a pre-race rest day on D-2 or D-1.
suggestedChanges: Insert at least one full rest day in the final 3-4 days before the Sep 14 A-priority Olympic triathlon (e.g., on Sep 12 or Sep 13).
